sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐秘。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: If you grew up watching Warner Brothers cartoons, and I really, really hope you did,
sentences.zh: 如果你是在看华纳兄弟动画片中长大的，而且我真的、真的很希望你是，

sentences.en: you might remember seeing the words,
sentences.zh: 你可能记得看到过这样几个字：

sentences.en: Directed by Chuck Jones, in big letters in the opening credits.
sentences.zh: 导演：查克·琼斯，片头字幕里有很大的字。

sentences.en: Chuck Jones worked for decades on cartoons like Looney Tunes,
sentences.zh: 查克·琼斯为《乐一通》之类的动画工作了几十年，

sentences.en: from the 1930s until his death in 2002.
sentences.zh: 从20世纪30年代一直到他2002年逝世。

sentences.en: In addition to being a director, he was also an animator.
sentences.zh: 除了担任导演，他也是一名动画师。

sentences.en: He gave Bugs Bunny that cocky slouch.
sentences.zh: 他赋予了兔八哥那种傲慢的站姿。

sentences.en: He gave Daffy Duck those mischievous eyes.
sentences.zh: 他赋予了达菲鸭那种淘气的眼神。

sentences.en: I think Bugs Bunny's more mischievous.
sentences.zh: 我觉得兔八哥更淘气。

sentences.en: Daffy Duck is insane.
sentences.zh: 达菲鸭简直是个疯子。

sentences.en: He made a mute Wile E.
sentences.zh: 他让一个不会说话的歪心狼（Wile E.）

sentences.en: Coyote hold up signs that commented
sentences.zh: 举起牌子，评论着

sentences.en: on the sad irony of his cartoon life.
sentences.zh: 他那滑稽人生中悲伤的讽刺意味。

sentences.en: In 1996, Jones accepted an Academy Award for Lifetime Achievement.
sentences.zh: 1996年，琼斯接受了奥斯卡终身成就奖。

sentences.en: Well, I stand guilty before the world of directing over 300 cartoons
sentences.zh: 嗯，在过去的50到60年里，

sentences.en: in the last 50 or 60 years.
sentences.zh: 我导演了300多部动画片，对此我难辞其咎。

sentences.en: Hopefully, this means you've forgiven me.
sentences.zh: 希望这意味着你们已经原谅了我。

sentences.en: Chuck Jones is the name most people remember when they think about those cartoons.
sentences.zh: 当人们想起那些动画片时，查克·琼斯是大多数人记住的名字。

sentences.en: But I want to talk about another guy, an artist who worked with Chuck Jones,
sentences.zh: 但我想谈谈另一个人，一个曾与查克·琼斯合作过的艺术家，

sentences.en: a guy who wasn't just important to Looney Tunes.
sentences.zh: 一个不仅对《乐一通》至关重要的人。

sentences.en: He changed the entire art of animation.
sentences.zh: 他改变了整个动画艺术。

sentences.en: Yeah, the amazing thing about this guy is that he never drew Bugs Bunny
sentences.zh: 是的，这家伙最了不起的地方在于他从未画过兔八哥

sentences.en: or Elmer Fudd or Yosemite Sam or any of those characters.
sentences.zh: 或埃尔默·福德或约塞米蒂·萨姆或任何这些角色。

sentences.en: He drew the backgrounds behind those characters.
sentences.zh: 他画的是那些角色身后的背景。

sentences.en: So if you think of, like, have you ever seen Duck Dodgers in the 24th and a half century?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想一想，比如，你看过《二十四又二分之一世纪的达菲鸭》吗？

sentences.en: Daffy Duck lands on this weird, futuristic planet.
sentences.zh: 达菲鸭降落在一个奇怪的、充满未来感的星球上。

sentences.en: Or, you know, the Roadrunner cartoons, that jagged, bright, abstract desert.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，《跑步机》（Roadrunner）动画片，那种参差不齐、色彩明亮、抽象的沙漠。

sentences.en: That is the work of Maurice Noble.
sentences.zh: 那是莫里斯·诺布尔的作品。

sentences.en: Here helping us tell this story is reporter Eric Molenski.
sentences.zh: 在这里帮我们讲述这个故事的是记者埃里克·莫伦斯基。

sentences.en: Hey.
sentences.zh: 嘿。

sentences.en: Eric used to work in animation as a storyboard artist on The Rugrats
sentences.zh: 埃里克过去曾在动画界工作，担任过《小淘气》的的分镜头画师

sentences.en: and a couple of other cartoons for Nickelodeon.
sentences.zh: 以及尼克国际儿童频道的一些其他动画片。

sentences.en: Yeah, late 90s, early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 对，90年代末，2000年代初。

sentences.en: So break down for us what the layout artist does in the whole animation process.
sentences.zh: 所以请为我们剖析一下，布局画师在整个动画制作过程中扮演什么角色。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, so today, like in a, you know, a TV show, you would start out with a script.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以今天，就像在，你知道的，一部电视剧里，你通常会从一个剧本开始。

sentences.en: Or in the case of Looney Tunes, it probably, they'd start drawing story sketches
sentences.zh: 或者在《乐一通》的情况下，可能，他们会开始画故事草图

sentences.en: to figure out the gags and the camera angles and stuff.
sentences.zh: 来构思笑料和镜头角度之类的东西。

sentences.en: And then before the animation starts, the background designer or layout artist
sentences.zh: 然后，在动画开始制作之前，背景设计师或布局画师

sentences.en: has the first crack at drawing this world.
sentences.zh: 拥有绘制这个世界的首个机会。

sentences.en: And those drawings are then later painted in by someone else.
sentences.zh: 而这些画作随后会由其他人进行上色。

sentences.en: But, you know, a layout artist like Maurice Noble, who's really accomplished,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，像莫里斯·诺布尔这样卓有成就的布局画师，

sentences.en: would actually have a say in the color choices as well.
sentences.zh: 实际上对色彩的选择也拥有发言权。

sentences.en: And so this is actually really important.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上非常重要。

sentences.en: So imagine you're watching a cartoon.
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下你正在看一部动画片。

sentences.en: And, you know, the layout or the, you know, the background is sometimes the first image
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，布局或者，你知道的，背景有时是你看到的第一个画面

sentences.en: that you see.
sentences.zh: 它只是在屏幕上闪现了一秒钟。

sentences.en: It just pops on screen for a second.
sentences.zh: 而你的大脑需要瞬间识别出你身处何地，以及你应该感受到什么情绪。

sentences.en: And your brain needs to instantly register where you are and what mood you're supposed to feel.
sentences.zh: 所以，比如，你知道的，假设你正在看一部《走鹃》动画片。

sentences.en: So, like, you know, let's say you're watching a Roadrunner cartoon.
sentences.zh: 镜头切到一个大圆石，它栖息在一个非常高、非常窄的悬崖顶上。

sentences.en: You cut to this big boulder that's perched on top of a really high, narrow cliff.
sentences.zh: 你马上就会为那只土狼感到担忧。

sentences.en: You're going to immediately feel dread for the coyote.
sentences.zh: 所以布局画师有点像喜剧双人组里的捧哏，

sentences.en: So the layout artist is kind of like the straight man in the comedy duo,
sentences.zh: 为负责搞笑的动画师铺垫笑料。

sentences.en: setting up the gag for the animator who gets to be, you know, the funny guy.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 而且他们得不到太多认可。

sentences.en: And they don't get much credit.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们字面意思上就在背景里。

sentences.en: I mean, they're literally in the background.
sentences.zh: 他们在创作这些煞费苦心的艺术品，然后别人直接把画作

sentences.en: They're creating this painstaking work of art before somebody else plops their drawings
sentences.zh: 叠放在它上面。

sentences.en: right on top of it.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须克制自己的傲慢。

sentences.en: So you have to keep your ego in check.
sentences.zh: 莫里斯·诺布尔的大部分职业生涯都是为华纳兄弟工作的。

sentences.en: Maurice Noble spent most of his career working for Warner Brothers.
sentences.zh: 但他一开始并不是画那些古怪的动画片的。

sentences.en: But he didn't start out doing, you know, wacky cartoons.
sentences.zh: 作为一个年轻人，他想成为一名绘制沙漠风景的美术家。

sentences.en: As a young man, he wanted to be a fine artist painting desert landscapes.
sentences.zh: 当他从艺术学校毕业时，莫里斯在华特迪士尼动画工作室找到了工作。

sentences.en: When he graduated art school, Maurice found work at Walt Disney Studios.
sentences.zh: 他的第一份工作是画一个苹果。

sentences.en: His first job was painting an apple.
sentences.zh: 他说这是一个非常乏味的过程，一个非常严格的过程，就是把

sentences.en: And he said it was very sort of a tedious process, a very exacting process of just putting the
sentences.zh: 颜色一点点加上去以进行匹配。

sentences.en: colors down gradually to match.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他当时并不这么觉得，但这绝对在创作上束缚了他。

sentences.en: You know, he didn't think so at the moment, but it was definitely hampering him creatively.
sentences.zh: 这是鲍勃·麦金农，他写了一本关于莫里斯·诺布尔的传记。

sentences.en: This is Bob McKinnon, who wrote a biography of Maurice Noble.
sentences.zh: 他说，尽管迪士尼长片有这些非常逼真且细腻的背景，

sentences.en: He says that even though Disney feature films had these really realistic and subtle backgrounds,
sentences.zh: 你知道，你能看到树上的每一片叶子或门把手上的反光，

sentences.en: you know, you see every leaf on a tree or the shine on a doorknob,
sentences.zh: 但莫里斯觉得他在自甘堕落，在商业艺术上挥霍自己的才华。

sentences.en: Maurice felt like he was slumming it, squandering his talent on commercial art.
sentences.zh: 1941年，迪士尼工作室因一场罢工而分裂。

sentences.en: In 1941, Disney Studios was torn apart by a strike.
sentences.zh: 艺术家们想要建立一个工会，而华特对这次罢工非常、非常介意。

sentences.en: The artist wanted to create a union, and Walt took the walk out very, very personally.
sentences.zh: 当罢工结束后，他解雇了所有与罢工相关的人，包括莫里斯·诺布尔。

sentences.en: When it was over, he got rid of anyone associated with the strike, including Maurice Noble.
sentences.zh: 我想如果罢工没有发生，他说他在迪士尼会有一份干一辈子的工作。

sentences.en: I think if the strike had not happened, he said he would have had a job for a lifetime at Disney.
sentences.zh: 我想他会在那里永远待下去。

sentences.en: I think he would have stayed there forever.
sentences.zh: 但莫里斯并没有失业多久。

sentences.en: But Maurice wasn't unemployed for long.
sentences.zh: 第二次世界大战爆发了，他被征召入伍，进入了一个制作宣传片的部队，片中有一个

sentences.en: World War II broke out, and he was drafted into a unit that made propaganda films featuring
sentences.zh: 名为“二等兵斯纳富”的卡通角色。

sentences.en: a cartoon character named Private Snafu.
sentences.zh: 你会叫你闭嘴。

sentences.en: You will tell you to shut up.
sentences.zh: 我可不是个笨蛋，我也不会落入陷阱。

sentences.en: I ain't no boob and I won't be trapped.
sentences.zh: 正如你从那个电影片段中大概能看出来的，里面有梅尔·布兰科非常独特的配音，

sentences.en: As you can probably tell from that film clip, which has the very distinct voice of Mel Blanc in it,
sentences.zh: 那个宣传片摄制组里全是来自华纳兄弟的人，包括查克·琼斯。

sentences.en: the propaganda film crew was full of people from Warner Brothers, including Chuck Jones.
sentences.zh: 所以我还采访了托德·保尔森，他正在写一本关于莫里斯艺术作品的书。

sentences.en: So I also talked with Todd Paulson, who's working on a book about Maurice's artwork.
sentences.zh: 他说莫里斯发现他们的风格非常解放。

sentences.en: And he says Maurice found their style to be liberating.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有参与那些军队电影的人绝对都能够最终表达自我。

sentences.en: You know, everybody that was involved with those films for the Army definitely were able to finally express themselves.
sentences.zh: 然后战争结束后，他们为莫里斯安排了一份在华纳兄弟工作的工作。

sentences.en: And then after the war, they got Maurice a job working at Warner Brothers.
sentences.zh: 他说，我当时在冒汗，他说。

sentences.en: He says, I was sweating, he said.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道他对那项特定的业务了解得有多么少。

sentences.en: No one knew how little he knew about that particular end of the business.
sentences.zh: 据他所能，他当时完全是在即兴摸索。

sentences.en: And according to him, he was flying by the seat of his pants.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他以前做过布局，但我的意思是，他们当时每年要疯狂制作大约30部短片。

sentences.en: I mean, he had done layouts before, but I mean, they were cranking out something like 30 short films per year.
sentences.zh: 为了让你感受一下那是多么疯狂。

sentences.en: And just to give you a sense of how crazy that is.
sentences.zh: 所以今天，你知道的，或者至少当我还在电视界工作时，你知道，我们会把分镜头脚本寄到韩国。

sentences.en: So today, you know, or at least when I worked in TV, you know, we would ship our storyboards to Korea.
sentences.zh: 今天，他们可能只会，你知道，把它们发电子邮件到韩国，在那里，你知道，更廉价的劳动力会完成动画的填充。

sentences.en: Today, they would probably just, you know, email them to Korea where, you know, cheaper labor will fill in the animation.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以使用像Flash这样的基于计算机的程序来加速工作流程。

sentences.en: Or you could use a computer-based program like Flash to speed up the workflow.
sentences.zh: 而这仅仅是为了制作一季的22集。

sentences.en: And that's just to make 22 episodes for a season.
sentences.zh: 这些家伙在做更多的工作，而且全部都是手工完成的。

sentences.en: These guys are doing more work and doing it all by hand.
sentences.zh: 与他为迪士尼画的那个第一个煞费苦心般逼真的苹果不同，

sentences.en: Unlike that first painstakingly realistic apple that he painted for Disney,
sentences.zh: 莫里斯·诺布尔开始接受这样一种观念：背景应该更扁平、更具卡通感。

sentences.en: Maurice Noble comes to embrace the idea that backgrounds should be flatter and more cartoonish.
sentences.zh: 更像那些角色。

sentences.en: More like the characters.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，另一个例子是《森林王子》。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, like another example would be Jungle Book.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，回到迪士尼，这是我最喜欢的电影之一，因为动画简直太棒了。

sentences.en: I mean, going back to Disney, it's one of my favorite movies because the animation is totally amazing.
sentences.zh: 而且它与那些演员的配音完美地契合。

sentences.en: And it matches so beautifully the voices of those actors.
sentences.zh: 但我一直对一件事感到困扰，那就是角色有点扁平且呈二维感。

sentences.en: But I've always been bothered by the fact that the characters are kind of flat and 2D.
sentences.zh: 但森林的呈现却有着这些微妙的色彩和，你知道的，光影以及具有三维阴影的树木。

sentences.en: But the jungle is rendered with these subtle colors and, you know, lighting and the trees of three-dimensional shading.
sentences.zh: 我始终无法真正地说服自己相信这些角色实际上生活在那个世界里。

sentences.en: And I could never really suspend my disbelief that those characters are actually living in that world.
sentences.zh: 莫里斯·诺布尔对迪士尼电影也有同样的感受。

sentences.en: And Maurice Noble felt the same way about Disney filMs.
sentences.zh: 他一直认为动画是一种扁平的、风格化的媒介，所以他希望背景能够支撑这一点。

sentences.en: He always felt animation was a flat, stylized medium, so he wanted the backgrounds to support that.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢使用喷笔。

sentences.en: He didn't like the use of airbrush.
sentences.zh: 他总觉得其他一些工作室的背景与角色在针锋相对。

sentences.en: He always felt the backgrounds that some other studios were fighting the characters.
sentences.zh: 人们会走到他面前说，哦，你是受莫奈以及这啊那啊的启发。

sentences.en: And people would come up to him and say, oh, you were inspired by Monet and this and that.
sentences.zh: 而他说，我不是那样想的。

sentences.en: And he says, I don't think that way.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们是在一个完全崭新的媒介中工作。

sentences.en: He says, we're working in a completely new medium.
sentences.zh: 这是一个完全独特的艺术形式。

sentences.en: This is a completely unique art form.
sentences.zh: 莫里斯最终改变了华纳兄弟正在做的事情，因为他不断推陈出新，增强背景的卡通感

sentences.en: And Maurice ends up changing what Warner Brothers was doing because he's pushing the cartooniness of the backgrounds
sentences.zh: 直到它们拥有与兔八哥相同的俏皮或达菲鸭那种疯狂的神经质。

sentences.en: until they have the same sass as Bugs Bunny or the delusional insanity of Daffy Duck.
sentences.zh: 就像在《走鹃》动画片中，土狼真正的对头其实并不是走鹃。

sentences.en: Like in the Roadrunner cartoons, the coyote's real antagonist isn't really the Roadrunner.
sentences.zh: 而是沙漠景观和，你知道的，艾克米公司，它们合谋让他的生活苦不堪言。

sentences.en: It's the desert landscape and, you know, the Acme Corporation, which are conspiring to make his life miserable.
sentences.zh: 哔哔。

sentences.en: Meep, meep.
sentences.zh: 在他去之前制作的早期《走鹃》动画片，有那么几部，它们稍微更逼真一些。

sentences.en: The earlier Roadrunner cartoons that were done before he got there, there's a few of them, they're a little more realistic.
sentences.zh: 它们稍微更直截了当一些。

sentences.en: They're a little more just straight ahead.
sentences.zh: 而当他到了那里之后，他开始运用所有这些不同的技术。

sentences.en: And when he got there, he started to use all these different techniques.
sentences.zh: 随着他的推进，他会使用这些他所谓的“错位色彩”，即岩石的线条与它们背后的颜色无法对齐。

sentences.en: And as he went along, he would have these, what he called, off-registration colors where the lines of the rocks wouldn't line up with the color behind them.
sentences.zh: 他说那是为了给你一种热浪扭曲的视觉感。

sentences.en: And he said that was to give you a heat shimmer.
sentences.zh: 他对这再熟悉不过了，因为他在新墨西哥州长大。

sentences.en: Which he knew all about because he grew up in New Mexico.
sentences.zh: 他在那种环境下长大。

sentences.en: He grew up in that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他在岩石中玩耍，他亲眼目睹过。

sentences.en: He played in the rocks and he saw it.
sentences.zh: 我确信所有这些都影响了他制作《走鹃》动画时对沙漠的看法。

sentences.en: I'm sure all that influenced his take on the deserts when he did the Roadrunner cartoons.
sentences.zh: 这就是莫里斯·诺布尔如何成为布局设计界英雄的历程。

sentences.en: And this is how Maurice Noble becomes a hero to layout designers.
sentences.zh: 记住，他的作品不应该喧宾夺主、抢走角色的风头。

sentences.en: Remember, his work is not supposed to detract from the characters.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，布局应该支撑动画并使其脱颖而出。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, the layouts are supposed to support the animation and make it stand out.
sentences.zh: 而他出色地做到了这一点。

sentences.en: And he does that brilliantly.
sentences.zh: 但他也发展出了一种独特且极具辨识度的风格。

sentences.en: But he also develops a unique and recognizable style.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这几乎就像他为一场演出搭建了一个舞台，但这个舞台在向观众眨眼。

sentences.en: I mean, it's almost like he built a stage for a show, but the stage is winking at the audience.
sentences.zh: 所以我曾在加州艺术学院学习动画。

sentences.en: So I studied animation at CalArts.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会看像《二十四又二分之一世纪的达菲鸭》这样的动画片。

sentences.en: And so we'd be watching a cartoon like Duck Dodgers in the 24th and a half century.
sentences.zh: 我们会放声大笑，因为达菲鸭降落在了X星球上，而莫里斯把云朵和树木画成了巨大的X形状。

sentences.en: And we would burst out laughing because Daffy Duck had landed on Planet X and Maurice had drawn the clouds and the trees in the shape of giant X's.
sentences.zh: 我敢打赌，如果我们沿着那些行星走，就会找到X星球。

sentences.en: I'll just bet that if we follow those planets, we'll find Planet X.
sentences.zh: 查德，我是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: Chad, how do I do it?
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 随着诺布尔逐渐崭露头角，他开始在一些电影中获得联合导演的署名。

sentences.en: As Noble is coming into his own, he's starting to get co-director credit on some of the filMs.
sentences.zh: 但查克·琼斯仍然收获了大部分的赞誉。

sentences.en: But Chuck Jones is still reaping most of the acclaim.
sentences.zh: 托德·保尔森是莫里斯的门生之一，他说这在60年代他们在米高梅工作时成为了他们之间紧张关系的导火索。

sentences.en: Todd Polson, one of Maurice's protégés, says that this became a point of tension between them in the 60s when they were working at MGM.
sentences.zh: 这是一种工作关系。

sentences.en: It was a working relationship.
sentences.zh: 随着查克越来越成功，尤其是在60年代，这种关系变得越来越紧张。

sentences.en: And it became more and more strained as Chuck became more and more successful, especially in the 60s.
sentences.zh: 当他们制作《点与线》时，这种矛盾达到了顶峰。

sentences.en: And that came to a head when they made Dot in the Line.
sentences.zh: 《点与线》是一部儿童读物的改编作品。

sentences.en: The Dot in the Line was an adaptation of a children's book.
sentences.zh: 《点与线》改编自一本儿童读物。

sentences.en: And it was about a dot that falls in love with a line, and it's a story of their romance.
sentences.zh: 故事讲的是一个圆点爱上了一条直线，这是它们之间的浪漫爱情故事。

sentences.en: Chuck Jones was the director on the short, but he was having trouble figuring out how to adapt it.
sentences.zh: 查克·琼斯是这部短片的导演，但他一直在为如何改编它而发愁。

sentences.en: So the executives went to Maurice.
sentences.zh: 于是高管们找到了莫里斯。

sentences.en: And he said, well, if you don't involve Chuck, I can make this work for you.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，如果你们不让查克参与，我可以帮你们把这个做好。

sentences.en: And so Chuck brought the stuff in, threw it down on his desk, and stomped out.
sentences.zh: 于是查克把东西拿来，往桌上一摔，气冲冲地走了。

sentences.en: And Maurice wouldn't show him what he was working on.
sentences.zh: 而且莫里斯不让他看自己在做什么。

sentences.en: Once upon a time, there was a sensible, straight line who was hopelessly in love with a Dot.
sentences.zh: 从前，有一条循规蹈矩的直线，他无可救药地爱上了一个圆点。

sentences.en: You're the beginning and the end, the hub, the core, and the quintessence, he told her tenderly.
sentences.zh: “你是起点和终点，是枢纽、核心，是精髓，”他温柔地对她说。

sentences.en: But the frivolous Dot wasn't a bit interested, for she only had eyes for a wild and unkempt squiggle who never seemed to have anything on his mind at all.
sentences.zh: 但轻浮的圆点一点也不感兴趣，因为她满眼只有那个狂野而不修边幅的弯曲线条，他似乎满脑子不知道在想些什么。

sentences.en: It's a very charming film, but it's probably the most personal of all of Maurice's films because it's really just him on the screen.
sentences.zh: 这是一部非常迷人的电影，但它可能是莫里斯所有作品中最具个人色彩的一部，因为银幕上展现的真的就是他自己。

sentences.en: It's pure graphics.
sentences.zh: 这是纯粹的图形艺术。

sentences.en: There's no classic characters, as you might think of them.
sentences.zh: 里面没有你通常认为的那些经典角色。

sentences.en: It's just dots, lines.
sentences.zh: 只有点和线。

sentences.en: It's purely abstract, but really beautiful.
sentences.zh: 它完全是抽象的，但真的很美。

sentences.en: The film is this pure distillation of Maurice's work.
sentences.zh: 这部电影堪称莫里斯作品的纯粹精髓。

sentences.en: He's telling a story, creating emotions and humor with just basic shapes and colors.
sentences.zh: 他仅用最基础的形状和色彩，就在讲述故事、创造情绪和幽默。

sentences.en: But Chuck Jones still got director credit.
sentences.zh: 但查克·琼斯还是挂名了导演。

sentences.en: And of course, it won the Oscar, but he said that Chuck didn't ever thank him.
sentences.zh: 当然，这部片子赢得了奥斯卡奖，但他却说查克从来没向他道过谢。

sentences.en: And Todd says that even though everyone knew it was Maurice's film, Maurice wasn't invited to the Oscars.
sentences.zh: 托德说，尽管大家都知道这是莫里斯的电影，但莫里斯却没有被邀请去奥斯卡颁奖典礼。

sentences.en: So Chuck Jones and Maurice Noble kept working together.
sentences.zh: 所以查克·琼斯和莫里斯·诺贝尔继续合作。

sentences.en: They worked on How the Grinch Stole Christmas and a bunch of other Dr. Seuss adaptations.
sentences.zh: 他们合作了《圣诞怪杰》以及一堆其他的苏斯博士作品改编。

sentences.en: But they fell out of touch for about 20 years until the early 1990s, when Warner Brothers reunited them to make cartoons that played before feature filMs.
sentences.zh: 但他们失联了大约20年，直到20世纪90年代初，华纳兄弟让他们重新聚首，制作在长片上映前播出的动画短片。

sentences.en: They hired a bunch of young artists who just graduated from CalArts.
sentences.zh: 他们雇了一批刚从加州艺术学院毕业的年轻艺术家。

sentences.en: And one of them was Scott Morse.
sentences.zh: 斯科特·莫斯就是其中之一。

sentences.en: Maurice Noble, Maurice Noble, where do I know that from?
sentences.zh: 莫里斯·诺贝尔，莫里斯·诺贝尔，我怎么觉得这个名字这么耳熟？

sentences.en: I was like, oh, it's because it was one of the names that preceded, directed by Charles M.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，哦，因为在我有生之年每天看的所有动画片里，

sentences.en: Jones,
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·M·琼斯

sentences.en: on all of the cartoons that I grew up watching every day of my life.
sentences.zh: 导演的名字前面都有他。

sentences.en: One of the first lessons that Scott learned was that Maurice's fantastic backgrounds were not just invented out of thin air.
sentences.zh: 斯科特学到的第一课之一，就是莫里斯那些奇妙的背景并非凭空捏造。

sentences.en: Maurice did a ton of research.
sentences.zh: 莫里斯做过大量的调研。

sentences.en: Everything he exaggerated was based on something in the real world.
sentences.zh: 他夸张的一切都以现实世界中的事物为基础。

sentences.en: You'd get an assignment like, oh, you know, Bugs Bunny's going to be stuck on a desert island or stuck on a jungle island.
sentences.zh: 你会接到这样的任务，比如，哦，你知道的，兔八哥要被困在荒岛上了，或者被困在丛林岛上了。

sentences.en: So there should be palm trees and there should be all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以应该有棕榈树，应该有所有这些东西。

sentences.en: And it's like, OK, great.
sentences.zh: 然后就像是，行，太棒了。

sentences.en: And I'd come back with a drawing and he'd be like, what is this?
sentences.zh: 我带着画回来，他就会说，这是什么？

sentences.en: And I'm like, oh, they're palm trees.
sentences.zh: 我说，哦，它们是棕榈树。

sentences.en: And he's like, those are stuckas.
sentences.zh: 他说，那些是刺葵。

sentences.en: What were you looking at?
sentences.zh: 你画的时候看的是什么？

sentences.en: And it's like, well, there's a palm tree right out the window.
sentences.zh: 我就说，嗯，窗外就有一棵棕榈树。

sentences.en: He's like, that's a stucka.
sentences.zh: 他说，那是刺葵。

sentences.en: You got to learn your trees.
sentences.zh: 你得好好认识一下树。

sentences.en: But Maurice wasn't really that gruff.
sentences.zh: 但莫里斯其实并没有那么严厉粗暴。

sentences.en: After work, he talked to these 22-year-old animators like he was just one of the guys.
sentences.zh: 下班后，他跟这些22岁的动画师聊天时就像哥们儿一样随和。

sentences.en: He'd be like, let's go to the baseball game.
sentences.zh: 他会说，我们去看棒球赛吧。

sentences.en: Let's go do this other thing.
sentences.zh: 我们去干点别的吧。

sentences.en: You know, we should go to a museum.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们应该去趟博物馆。

sentences.en: Pretty soon you realize he's more like your grandpa, who is just a really cool guy to hang out with.
sentences.zh: 很快你就会发现他更像你的爷爷，一个在一起相处时非常酷的人。

sentences.en: So Scott Morse and this group of artists became known as the Noble Boys.
sentences.zh: 于是斯科特·莫斯和这群艺术家被称为“诺贝尔男孩”。

sentences.en: And Maurice pushed them to develop their own style.
sentences.zh: 莫里斯鼓励他们发展自己的风格。

sentences.en: But his sensibility really seeped into their work.
sentences.zh: 但他的审美趣味确实渗透到了他们的作品中。

sentences.en: Like, Scott is at Pixar now, which is the home of 3D animation,
sentences.zh: 比如，斯科特现在在皮克斯，那是3D动画的大本营，

sentences.en: which you would think is the complete opposite of, you know, the flat landscapes of Looney Tunes.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得这与《乐一通》里那些平面的风景完全相反。

sentences.en: But you can really see Maurice's influence on the Pixar films if you look for it.
sentences.zh: 但如果你仔细寻找，真的能看到莫里斯对皮克斯电影的影响。

sentences.en: Like the film Up.
sentences.zh: 比如电影《飞屋环游记》。

sentences.en: Think about that house carried by a massive amount of balloons that lands on the very edge of a cliff.
sentences.zh: 想想那座被大量气球带着、最后降落在悬崖边上的房子。

sentences.en: Or in Wally, this cute little robot is scooting around these big, menacing towers of garbage.
sentences.zh: 或者在《机器人总动员》里，这个可爱的小机器人在巨大的、充满威胁的垃圾塔之间穿梭。

sentences.en: You know, those are layouts that make you smile.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那些都是能让你会心一笑的构图。

sentences.en: And that's classic Maurice.
sentences.zh: 这就是典型的莫里斯风格。

sentences.en: In May of 2001, the Noble Boys were reunited one last time.
sentences.zh: 2001年5月，“诺贝尔男孩”们最后一次聚在了一起。

sentences.en: We all got, you know, the call that Maurice, he was in hospice basically at home.
sentences.zh: 我们都接到了电话，得知莫里斯基本上在家里接受临终关怀。

sentences.en: It was just natural causes that he was dying of.
sentences.zh: 他得的是自然衰老引发的病症，生命正在走向尽头。

sentences.en: And he was pretty sure, you know, everybody was pretty sure that that night was going to maybe be the last night.
sentences.zh: 而且他很确定，大家都挺确信那天晚上可能是最后一个晚上了。

sentences.en: So we all came over and hung out with him.
sentences.zh: 所以我们都赶了过来，陪伴在他身边。

sentences.en: And Chuck Jones did call that night.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上查克·琼斯确实打来过电话。

sentences.en: And I remember being in the room with Maurice and somebody brought him the phone.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时我和莫里斯在同一个房间里，有人把电话递给了他。

sentences.en: I was like, Chuck's on the phone.
sentences.zh: 我说，查克在电话里。

sentences.en: And Maurice was like, okay, I'll talk to him.
sentences.zh: 莫里斯说，好吧，我和他说。

sentences.en: And we all knew for a fact that they hadn't really talked for months, if not a couple of years at that point.
sentences.zh: 我们都确切地知道，到那个时候，他们其实已经好几个月甚至好几年没怎么说过话了。

sentences.en: And I just heard Maurice's side of the conversation.
sentences.zh: 我只听到了莫里斯那边的对话内容。

sentences.en: But, you know, you could definitely tell that they were, they had put everything behind them and they were friends.
sentences.zh: 但是，你绝对能听出来他们已经把一切都抛在脑后了，他们是朋友。

sentences.en: You know, and it was nice.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这感觉很好。

sentences.en: And again, I don't know exactly what Chuck said on the other end of that line,
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我不知道查克在电话那头具体说了什么，

sentences.en: but it was a very sweet moment to be able to see that and know that people could go through a lot together in life and still have respect for each other, you know,
sentences.zh: 但能看到这一幕真的很温馨，也让人明白人们在生活中可以经历很多风雨，却依然能互相尊重，你知道的，

sentences.en: up to the last minute.
sentences.zh: 直到最后一刻。

sentences.en: And kind of celebrate what they had created together.
sentences.zh: 并且共同庆祝他们曾经一起创造的成就。

sentences.en: To some extent, Maurice saw the Noble Boys as his real legacy.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上，莫里斯将“诺贝尔男孩”视为他真正的遗产。

sentences.en: He was proud of the fact that they had blossomed into well-rounded artists.
sentences.zh: 他为他们成长为成熟全面的艺术家而感到骄傲。

sentences.en: If Maurice could leave behind this idea in other people to do their own thing, we would never be in the background like he was.
sentences.zh: 如果莫里斯能在其他人心中留下这种坚持做自己的理念，我们就永远不会像他那样退居幕后。

sentences.en: But it was a beautiful, beautiful background.
sentences.zh: 但那是一个美丽的、无与伦比的幕后。

sentences.en: I actually met Maurice Noble once.
sentences.zh: 我其实见过莫里斯·诺贝尔一次。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah?
sentences.zh: 哦，是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I went to CalArts and he came into our class on a, it was like a Monday night.
sentences.zh: 我在加州艺术学院上学时，他来过我们的课堂，那是某个星期一的晚上。

sentences.en: And I had happened to have gone to the opera the day before on, you know, the weekend.
sentences.zh: 而我刚好在头一天，也就是周末的时候去听了歌剧。

sentences.en: And I was thinking about how often those guys made fun of opera in their cartoons.
sentences.zh: 我当时就在想，这群家伙在他们的动画里拿歌剧开玩笑的频率还挺高的。

sentences.en: I've killed the rabbit.
sentences.zh: 我杀了那只兔子。

sentences.en: Poor widow bunny.
sentences.zh: 可怜的寡妇兔。

sentences.en: Poor widow rabbit.
sentences.zh: 可怜的寡妇兔子。

sentences.en: And I asked him, you know, did you guys actually go to the opera regularly?
sentences.zh: 我问他，你们当时真的是经常去看歌剧吗？

sentences.en: Or were you just kind of making fun of it as a sort of, you know, highfalutin cultural institution?
sentences.zh: 还是只是把它当成某种装腔作势的文化机构来开玩笑？

sentences.en: And he asked me, what opera did you see?
sentences.zh: 他反问我，你看的是哪部歌剧？

sentences.en: And I said, La Traviata?
sentences.zh: 我说，《茶花女》？

sentences.en: And he said, ah, Violetta, her death is beautiful.
sentences.zh: 他说，啊，薇奥莱塔，她的死太美了。

sentences.en: And that is a man who knew a good death when he saw it.
sentences.zh: 那是一个懂得欣赏何谓绝美之死的人。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Eric Malinsky with Sam Greenspan and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由埃里克·马林斯基与萨姆·格林斯潘以及我——罗曼·马尔斯共同制作。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 local public radio KALW in San Francisco and the American Institute of Architects in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 地方公共广播电台 KALW 以及旧金山美国建筑师学会的合作项目。

sentences.en: You can find the show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Facebook 上找到并关注本节目。

sentences.en: I tweet at Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我在推特上的账号是 Roman Mars。

sentences.en: But right now we have Maurice Noble layouts, the dot and the line short film, and the strikingly politically incorrect private snafu.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们有莫里斯·诺贝尔的构图手稿、短片《点与线》，以及那部政治不正确得惊人的大兵斯纳福短片。

sentences.en: It's really of its time.
sentences.zh: 它真的极具时代特色。
